{{Elections in Idaho}}
The '''2022 United States House of Representatives elections in Idaho''' will be held on November 8, 2022, to elect the two [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. representatives]] from the [[U.S. state|state]] of [[Idaho]], one from both of the state's [[Idaho's congressional districts|congressional districts]]. The elections coincided with [[2022 United States House of Representatives elections|other elections]] to the House of Representatives, [[2022 United States Senate elections|elections]] to the [[United States Senate]] and various [[2022 United States elections#State elections|state]] and [[2022 United States elections#Local elections|local elections]].
{{toclimit|2}}

{{see also|Idaho's 1st congressional district}}
The 1st district takes in the [[Idaho Panhandle]] and the western [[Boise metropolitan area|Boise area]]. The incumbent is Republican [[Russ Fulcher]], who was re-elected with 67.8% of the vote in 2020.<ref name="HPVT">{{cite web|last=Johnson|first=Cheryl L.|title=Statistics of the Congressional Election of November 3, 2020|url=http://history.house.gov/Institution/Election-Statistics/Election-Statistics/|publisher=[[Clerk of the United States House of Representatives|Clerk of the U.S. House of Representatives]]|date=February 28, 2019}}</ref>

{{see also|Idaho's 2nd congressional district}}
The 2nd district encompasses eastern and northern [[Boise]], as well as [[Eastern Idaho]]. The incumbent is Republican [[Mike Simpson]], who was re-elected with 64.1% of the vote in 2020.<ref name="HPVT"/>

===Republican primary===
====Candidates====
=====Nominee=====
*[[Mike Simpson]], incumbent U.S. Representative<ref name=ID02>{{cite news |last1=Moseley-Morris |first1=Kelcie |title=Mike Simpson, Bryan Smith will vie for seat to represent Idaho's 2nd congressional district |url=https://www.bigcountrynewsconnection.com/news/state/idaho/mike-simpson-bryan-smith-will-vie-for-seat-to-represent-idaho-s-2nd-congressional-district/article_8fbb0e22-d4a7-5546-9241-897825797af6.html |publisher=Big Country News |date=5 October 2021 |access-date=November 15, 2021 |archive-date=October 30, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211030205216/https://www.bigcountrynewsconnection.com/news/state/idaho/mike-simpson-bryan-smith-will-vie-for-seat-to-represent-idaho-s-2nd-congressional-district/article_8fbb0e22-d4a7-5546-9241-897825797af6.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

=====Eliminated in primary=====
*Flint Christensen<ref name="Candidate Filing Report">{{Cite web|url=https://sos.idaho.gov/elections/data/Candidate_Filing_Report.pdf|title=Candidate Filing Report}}</ref>
*Daniel Algiers Lucas Levy<ref name="Candidate Filing Report"/>
*Chris Porter<ref name="Candidate Filing Report"/>
*Bryan Smith, attorney, businessman, and candidate for this district in [[2014 United States House of Representatives elections in Idaho#District 2|2014]]<ref name=ID02/>

=====Withdrawn=====
*Matthew Sather<ref name="Sather">{{cite news |last1=Moseley-Morris |first1=Kelcie |title=Mike Simpson, Bryan Smith will vie for seat to represent Idaho’s 2nd congressional district |url=https://www.bigcountrynewsconnection.com/news/state/idaho/mike-simpson-bryan-smith-will-vie-for-seat-to-represent-idaho-s-2nd-congressional-district/article_8fbb0e22-d4a7-5546-9241-897825797af6.html |publisher=Big Country News |date=5 October 2021 |access-date=November 15, 2021 |archive-date=October 30, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211030205216/https://www.bigcountrynewsconnection.com/news/state/idaho/mike-simpson-bryan-smith-will-vie-for-seat-to-represent-idaho-s-2nd-congressional-district/article_8fbb0e22-d4a7-5546-9241-897825797af6.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>
